item.title: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown! — Fri Oct 23, 7:30 PM — Owen Theatre
item.description:
MHU Theatre Arts Department brings an entertaining musical filled with family comedy, wise cracking characters, and heart-warming moments. From October 23-25 at Owen Theatre, a talented cast of theatre arts students is thrilled to share their hard work with you. The musical will be showing at 7:30 PM on Oct. 23, 2:30 PM and 7:30 PM on Oct. 24, and 2:30 PM on Oct. 25. Tickets to the show are $15 per person and can be purchased in person from the box office the night of the show or online at mhutheatre.ludus.com. Concessions will be available to purchase at any time before or during the show. All profits from concessions and ticket purchases will proceed to funding the theatre arts program at Mars Hill University for training the next generation of talented actors, singers, and tech professionals.

If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!
We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. item.title: Cemetery Loop Tr; a Saunter — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends **A Walk in the Park;** **This Week: *Cemetery Loop Tr:*** **DESCRIPTION;** *The Cemetery Loop Trail is a pleasant and short footpath which, when combined with the nearby Long Branch Trail offers a quick loop hike into a lesser-visited corner of Pisgah National Forest. Along the way there’s a decent variety of habitats to be seen. The main attraction is the 19th Century Cemetery which it passes at its far eastern extremity. Named the McCall Cemetery, it is named for the family and descendants of Samuel McCall who settled nearby in the late 1700’s. The cemetery sits in a serenely beautiful spot at the base of a low pine covered ridge.* Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises. Due to recent events, Ouija boards are no longer permitted. We are the Sloth Walking team: “We take our time… Up to 12 ppl are welcome to join. (Social ‘hour’ at 10 AM. item.title: 4-6 p.m. - Public Meeting for Portmanvilla Area Flood Mitigation Project (DRMF) — Thu Nov 12, 4:00 PM — - Town Hall Council Chambers 160 Midland Ave. Black Mountain NC 28711
item.description:
The Town of Black Mountain is advancing the Portmanvilla Area Flood Mitigation Project to reduce flood risks affecting nearby homes, roads, and community infrastructure. The project will evaluate improvements including culvert replacements, streambank stabilization, roadway restoration, and drainage system enhancements to help improve resilience during future storm events. The project focuses on three priority areas near Portmanvilla Road, Davis Drive, 6th Street, and 7th Street. A public meeting is scheduled for Thur., Nov. 12, 2026 from 4-6pm at Town Hall, 160 Midland Ave., Black Mountain, NC 28711 for citizen input and to ask questions about the project. This meeting is a drop-in event. https://www.townofblackmountain.org/calendar.aspx?EID=2378
Source: Town of Black Mountain
